finding: The fixed 6D complement graph has a 12-element dihedral automorphism subgroup. Its triangle, reflection-fixed contexts and a transitive 12-spoke orbit give a source-free symmetry reduction: a putative distinct-ray lift implementing the whole subgroup unitarily has an irreducible projector algebra; its projective action linearizes and its ordinary 6D representation is restricted to two types, one of which is excluded by a three-sign orthogonality argument. The remaining type is under exact analysis; numerical exploration is not a no-go.
remaining_gap: The complement could break some or all graph symmetries; neither the written symmetry reduction nor numerical exploration rules out an arbitrary C6 realization. Even a positive 75-ray lift would leave 25 QLS10 cells and full resolution to construct.
next_action: Independently check the literal automorphisms and publish the written symmetry classification; then exactify the remaining representation using rank-one eigenspaces and endpoint orthogonality.
